Weakly‑tuned, low‑magnitude neuron with no clear semantic content: its positive peaks land on ordinary mid‑clause syntactic "glue" tokens — determiners/auxiliaries/infinitival markers ("the", "be", "to") or a noun/modifier right before a complement ("country", "legislative", "allow") — and the same class of function words ("be", "that", "on") appears on the strongly negative side, so it appears to encode fine‑grained syntactic context rather than a distinct trigger.

Fires on the word that completes a familiar multi-word collocation/compound — the head noun or linking preposition predicted by the preceding modifier (e.g. "Fan→listing", "Facebook→Page", "European→project", "not-for→-profit", "board of directors→for", "oral arguments→in"); it is a lexical-completion detector rather than a topical one, and is inversely driven by other compound completions like "border wall", "climate change", "SoCs".
